The 720-pixel layout retains the gravity scene, timeline, buttons, object inspector, export panel and view options within the page width. The lower panels wrap below the viewport and remain readable. The orange sphere and green carrier remain visible; no horizontal crop or error state is visible.

The repaired.glb view at 1.500 s shows two separated gray/cyan figures with green arms; the left reference figure is outlined as selected. The inspector and controls are legible. The UI explicitly labels this local import as numerical status unknown and lacks a conformance report, consistent with the report's stated import boundary rather than a rendering error.

At 1.500 s, two gray uprights and their cyan members are visible: the shorter left rack includes an angled member, and the taller right rack shows five horizontal arms. The selected second object and timeline are legible. Local-import numerical status remains explicitly unknown. Neither rack is clipped by the viewport.

The front view at 0.000 s shows two distinct faceted clay-colored surfaces, with a blue upper region on the smaller left object. Both silhouettes and their material boundary are visible inside the frame; source and GLB identity text is legible below the viewer.

The side view at 0.000 s shows the clay-colored faceted silhouette and its central profile transition without clipping. The fixed side projection overlaps the two studio objects, so this image alone cannot establish separate visibility of both; the paired front capture does show both objects.

At the displayed 1.500 s front pose, both studio objects remain distinct and in frame. The smaller object's position differs from the initial front capture, while the blue/clay boundary remains coherent. This is a finite pose comparison, not a direct observation of continuous playback.

At 0.000 s the shell lies horizontally, with a broad clay-colored body on the left and a narrower blue segment on the right. Faceted shading and the color transition are visible; the full object remains inside the viewport.

The 0.000 s side view exposes the blue polygonal end face and surrounding blue facets in front of the clay-colored rear section. The silhouette is complete and separated from the page controls; no rendering error is visible.

At 1.500 s the shell's visible orientation and faceting differ from the initial front view while the clay/blue regional boundary remains intact. The entire shell stays in frame. The image supports this recorded pose only.

The fresh recovery's 0.000 s palette-repaired front view shows two separate faceted clay-colored objects, with a blue upper region on the smaller left object. Both silhouettes, the material legend and the source/GLB identities are visible without clipping or an error overlay.

At 0.000 s the side projection shows the larger clay-colored profile and its central transition. The objects overlap along this viewing direction, so this still alone does not establish separate visibility of both. The corresponding front capture shows both objects distinctly.

At the displayed 1.500 s pose, the smaller blue/clay object is displaced relative to its initial front capture while the larger clay-colored object remains visible to the right. Both stay in frame with coherent facets and regional color boundaries. This is a recorded pose observation only.

The 0.000 s ordinary composition contains two distinct upright tapered forms: a shorter blue-topped clay object on the left and a larger clay-colored form on the right. Both fill the viewport without being cropped, and the source/GLB identity text remains legible.

The side view at 0.000 s presents the taller clay-colored form with a complete faceted silhouette. Its projection occludes the other object along this direction; the paired front view establishes the two visible occurrences. No rendering error is visible.

At the displayed 1.500 s time, the two-object ordinary composition remains visually in the same arrangement as its initial front capture. Both silhouettes and the left object's blue/clay boundary remain clear. No motion is inferred merely from the timeline position.

The 0.000 s generated composition shows three separated blue-topped clay forms across the grid, with increasing visible width from left to right. All three are inside the frame. The material legend wraps below the viewport while remaining readable.

The side view aligns the generated forms in depth. A clay/blue foreground form and the staggered blue tips behind it are visible; overlapping projection limits independent silhouette assessment from this view alone. The front view shows the three separate occurrences.

At 1.500 s the three generated forms retain the same visible arrangement as the initial front capture. All are in frame and keep their blue/clay material transition. This still does not imply that the composition is animated.

The 0.000 s front view shows two separate horizontal tapered shells, each with a broad clay-colored left section and a narrow blue right section. Faceted shading and both complete silhouettes are visible without clipping.

At 0.000 s the side view shows the blue polygonal end face and clay-colored rear facets, with the two shells overlapping in the viewing direction. The end-face geometry is visible, while the paired front capture supplies their separate occurrence view.

At 1.500 s both horizontal shells remain visible and separated, with changed recorded pose/orientation relative to the initial front view. The blue/clay boundaries remain intact and the objects stay inside the frame. Release physics and continuous motion are left to the separate numerical evidence.
At 0.000 s a single faceted shell is visible with its blue end cap toward the camera and clay-colored body behind it. The model, fixed grid and identity text are visible without clipping.

The 0.000 s side view shows the shell's full tapered profile, blue at the narrow left end and clay-colored at the broad right end. Both material regions are distinct and the silhouette remains inside the fixed frame.

At 1.500 s the shell is higher in the fixed frame and presents a different orientation, with its blue cap toward the upper-left/front of the clay-colored body. It remains fully visible; no continuous-motion or impulse-accuracy claim is inferred from this still.

At 0.000 s the smaller shell is visible left of center, with a blue end region and clay-colored body. The wide fixed framing leaves substantial space around it; its small screen size limits geometric inspection but no clipping or error overlay is visible.
The 0.000 s side view shows the small tapered shell near the center with its blue narrow end to the left. The complete silhouette and color boundary remain discernible within the wide fixed view.

At 1.500 s the shell appears toward the upper-right relative to its initial front pose, with the blue cap and clay body still distinguishable. It remains inside the same displayed framing. This view establishes the recorded pose, not a complete trajectory.
At 0.000 s two separated shells are visible across the front view. Each has a blue end region and clay-colored body; both remain within the fixed frame with no error overlay.

The 0.000 s side view shows two tapered shells with depth/perspective separation, blue narrow ends to the left and clay-colored wider ends to the right. Both silhouettes and their regional material transitions are visible.

At 1.500 s both shells remain visible but present different orientations: the left shell is more horizontal, while the right shows a more upright face-on blue region. Their separation and material boundaries remain clear. Physical correctness is left to the separate numerical evidence.

At 0.000 s the small blue/clay shell is near the lower center above the grid. The trajectory-sized framing leaves substantial empty space above; the object is fully in frame, though its small size limits fine geometry inspection.
The 0.000 s side view shows the shell's narrow blue left segment and broad clay-colored right segment near the lower center. The whole tapered silhouette is visible inside the viewport.

At 1.500 s the small shell is substantially higher in the fixed frame and presents a more upright blue end face. It remains fully visible with readable pose/identity UI. The still does not independently prove continuous-time behavior or the impulse calculation.
